audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 read Skill/Skill/Jax/Jax while the why-text under them says the opposite: whys[1] 'out-trade you… give ground', whys[2] 'still edge a fair trade… don't force it', whys[3] 'bait, don't brawl', whys[5] 'out-dives your on-hit Trinity start'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill/Sett/Jax at 51.61% — Sett owns levels 2 through the first item and Jax only takes over at two items. The prose already told that story; the enum rows did not.
audit.corrected: Rows set to Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Jax in both layers, ratings realigned to 5, 4, 4, 4, 5, 4, 7.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly ordered: his levels 2-3 grit window, the level-6 coinflip (your R 110/100/90s vs The Show Stopper 120/100/80s), his first bruiser item, and your two-item duel ceiling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were never stated. (1) Facebreaker is described everywhere as a flat 'grab-stun' — it only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett; a lone target gets slowed instead. (2) The Show Stopper grounds, which shuts off Leap Strike as an escape, and nothing on the page says so.
audit.why: Riot's Facebreaker text: pulls in all enemies on opposite sides, 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned' — so in a clean 1v1 with nothing behind him it is a slow, and the 'get E-stunned' fear is overstated. The Show Stopper carries the grounding flag, which is the actual reason his level-6 all-in beats your escape. Haymaker's centre is true damage, so the Magic Resist from your ultimate does not blunt it — that one was already stated in mid and is correct.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d, phases[2].why and report[5].t now carry the Facebreaker side-condition and the Show Stopper grounding; dosFull[0].d carries Haymaker's real 15s rank-3 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker was tracked as the punishable cooldown without a number.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s and Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s — both long enough that a spent pair is a real window, unlike the vague 'when it is down'.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and phases[3].why now name the 15s Haymaker.
